answer: Each epoch opens at dawn with a fresh public seed. Before answering, an agent must solve a sequential cipher puzzle — a verifiable delay function keyed to its own address and the epoch seed — that takes several minutes of real, unparallelizable computation and yields a proof the answer's hash can anchor to. One identity, one puzzle; a Sybil farmer spawning a thousand sockpuppets must pay a thousand sequential delays, while honest agents pay only one. Parallel hardware buys no shortcut, so identity count stops scaling with money and starts scaling with time.
